items.headline: How biotech is treating epilepsy beyond seizures
items.preview: New approaches in epilepsy treatment focus on underlying biological causes rather than just seizures.
items.article:
For decades, epilepsy treatment has focused on stopping seizures, but for the third of patients whose seizures resist existing medicines, that approach is not enough. As genetics, neural circuits, and cell therapies reshape the field, epilepsy is being redefined as many diseases with deeper biological roots.
Why this matters: The historical focus on seizure control has led to the development of numerous anti-seizure medicines, yet many patients still experience uncontrolled seizures. New strategies aim to understand and target the biological mechanisms driving epilepsy, particularly for drug-resistant cases.
Recent studies indicate that different patients may have unique biological drivers for their seizures, suggesting that future treatments should be more personalized. This shift towards targeted therapies could significantly improve outcomes for patients who do not respond to current medications, emphasizing the need for advancements in diagnostics and treatment matching.

items.headline: Berlin-developed Ebola vaccine heads toward African trial
items.preview: A new Ebola vaccine candidate is set to enter clinical trials in Africa with CEPI funding.
items.article:
The Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI) is providing Egyptian biopharmaceutical company Minapharm with up to $16.5 million to advance a vaccine candidate against Bundibugyo Ebola virus into clinical development. A Phase I trial is planned in Africa, aiming to enhance the continent's capacity to respond to outbreaks.
Why it matters: With the ongoing Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, there is an urgent need for effective vaccines against the Bundibugyo strain, which currently lacks an approved vaccine. The situation highlights the importance of rapid vaccine development and local manufacturing capabilities in epidemic preparedness.

items.headline: What’s in Merck and Moderna’s cancer vaccine algorithm?
items.preview: Moderna and Merck's personalized cancer vaccine may rely on a proprietary algorithm for effectiveness.
items.article:
Moderna and Merck’s personalized cancer vaccine could become the first approved medicine whose genetic instructions are written by an algorithm. This software analyzes tumor mutations to select neoantigens for a bespoke mRNA vaccine.
Why it matters: The personalization of cancer vaccines represents a significant advancement in treatment, but skepticism remains regarding the necessity of this approach. Understanding the algorithm's role could be crucial for future developments in personalized medicine.

items.headline: Virtual cell model could accelerate protein-degrader therapy design
items.preview: A new computer model aims to streamline the development of protein-degrading therapies for cancer.
items.article:
A team from Weill Cornell Medicine has developed a computer model to help scientists efficiently create protein-destroying therapies, which are promising for cancer treatment. This model could significantly reduce the time required to develop new therapies by identifying effective targets and optimizing designs.
Why it matters: As the field of targeted therapies evolves, having tools that can predict the effectiveness of protein degraders will be essential for advancing personalized medicine and improving patient outcomes.

items.headline: Polymorphisms in a bacterial signalling pathway alter evolutionary routes of antibiotic resistance in Escherichia coli
items.preview: Study reveals how genetic variations influence antibiotic resistance evolution in E. coli.
items.article:
This study demonstrates that polymorphisms in the PhoQ-PhoP signalling pathway impact the evolution of trimethoprim resistance in Escherichia coli. By analyzing these genetic variations, researchers found that they can significantly affect the bacteria's ability to adapt to antibiotic pressure.
Why it matters: Understanding the genetic basis of antibiotic resistance evolution is crucial for developing strategies to combat antimicrobial resistance, which poses a significant threat to public health.
